analysis:
All changed files are test-only (ModelAutopilotTests.swift, ModelAutopilotUnloadTests.swift, and the new TransitionWatchdogTests.swift). They add no production code, wire surface, key handling, attestation or authorization logic, so I found no direct security regression.

What the tests cover: holdSeconds bounds in 0...86400 and only valid with a load target. Optional hold_seconds and detail fields on the wire. A watchdog-cancelled final unload failing as transition_stalled and clearing refusingNewWork. Existing consent, session/revision, selection, pin and busy checks (ModelAutopilotTests.swift lines 26-166, ModelAutopilotUnloadTests.swift lines 268-294).

The tests assert that provider-side validation fails closed against coordinator commands. This matches the trust model, in which the coordinator is trusted but its commands must still honor local consent and selection. They do not weaken any control.

Unverified because the production source is not in this batch: the actual implementations of ModelAutopilotPolicy.rejection, the holdSeconds enforcement, TransitionWatchdog and the superviseTransitions cancellation behavior. The TransitionWatchdogTests.swift unit (9e736450fb552fa7:0) was supplied only as a metadata/patch excerpt, so its content is only partly examined. The related production changes in other batches should be checked to confirm that a watchdog stall cannot leave residency state inconsistent, that the held/adopted model state is cleared, and that holdSeconds cannot be used to pin models beyond the consented selection (A-003/T-041 are not touched). The test files do not touch the prefix-cache threat T-041.
